'''Nedda Friberti''' (born 13 September 1913, date of death unknown) was an Italian [[Jewish refugees from German-occupied Europe in the United Kingdom|Jewish]] mathematician who fled Italy as a result of the German occupation of the [[Italian Social Republic|Italian Socialist Republic]] during [[World War II]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Holocaust Survivors and Victims Database – Search for Names Results |url=https://www.ushmm.org/online/hsv/person_advance_search.php?NameSearch__SourceSrchGrp=&NameSearch__ParentSourceId=&NameSearch__sort=name_primary_sort&NameSearch__lname=&NameSearch__lname_accuracy=&NameSearch__fname=&NameSearch__fname_accuracy=&NameSearch__lname_maiden=&NameSearch__lname_maiden_accuracy=&NameSearch__Query=&NameSearch__SourceId=27858&source_list=&NameSearch__year_birth=&NameSearch__year_birth_accuracy=&NameSearch__year_death=&NameSearch__year_death_accuracy=&NameSearch__year=&NameSearch__year_accuracy=&NameSearch__place=&NameSearch__place_accuracy=&NameSearch__place_IsGeoExpand_cb_0=&NameSearch__place_birth=&NameSearch__place_birth_accuracy=&NameSearch__place_birth_IsGeoExpand_cb_0=&NameSearch__place_prewar=&NameSearch__place_prewar_accuracy=&NameSearch__place_prewar_IsGeoExpand_cb_0=&NameSearch__place_wartime=&NameSearch__place_wartime_accuracy=&NameSearch__place_wartime_IsGeoExpand_cb_0=&NameSearch__place_death=&NameSearch__place_death_accuracy=&NameSearch__place_death_IsGeoExpand_cb_0=&NameSearch__meta_333=&NameSearch__meta_259=&MaxPageDocs=50&start_doc=5501 |access-date=2023-06-18 |website=www.ushmm.org}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Broggini |first=Renata |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NdAsAQAAIAAJ&q=Nedda+Friberti |title=Frontier of Hope: Jews from Italy Seek Refuge in Switzerland 1943–1945 |date=2003 |publisher=Ulrico Hoepli |isbn=978-88-203-3267-9 |language=en}}</ref> She was denied entry into the United States by the [[Emergency Committee in Aid of Displaced Foreign Scholars]].<ref>{{Citation |last=Gissi |first=Alessandra |chapter=Migranti, esiliate o rifugiate? : Le italiane nell'«intellectual wave» (Italia-Stati Uniti, 1938–1943) |date=26 May 2016 |chapter-url=http://books.openedition.org/aaccademia/895 |title=Lontane da casa : Donne italiane e diaspora globale dall'inizio del Novecento a oggi |pages=97–113 |editor-last=Luconi |editor-first=Stefano |access-date=2023-06-18 |series=Centro Altreitalie sulle Migrazioni Italiane |place=Torino |publisher=Accademia University Press |language=it |isbn=978-88-99200-09-1 |editor2-last=Varricchio |editor2-first=Mario}}</ref> In 1939, she was able to flee to [[Switzerland]] to escape persecution.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boissoneault |first=Lorraine |date=9 November 2017 |title=The Forgotten Women Scientists Who Fled the Holocaust for the United States |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/history/forgotten-women-scientists-who-fled-holocaust-united-states-180967166/ |access-date=2023-06-18 |website=Smithsonian Magazine |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Friberti was born in [[Trieste]] in 1913.<ref name=":0" /> She received a double degree in Mathematics and Physics. She worked as an assistant professor of Mathematics and Geometry at the [[Foligno|Technical Institute Leonardo da Vinci]] in 1937.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Gissi |first=Alessandra |title=«I should like very much to settle down in the US...». Italian women in the «intellectual wave» (1938–1943) in C. de la Guardia Herrero, E. Postigo Castellanos (eds.), Moving women and the United States: crossing the Atlantic |url=https://www.academia.edu/28892811 |journal=Publicaciones de la Universidad de Alcalá |volume=2016 |issue=Alcalá |pages=63–78}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bini |first=Gilberto |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tHC9EAAAQBAJ&q=nedda&pg=PA165 |title=Algebraic Geometry between Tradition and Future: An Italian Perspective |date=5 May 2023 |publisher=Springer Nature |isbn=978-981-19-8281-1 |language=en}}</ref>

Before teaching mathematics Friberti worked at the Geophysical Institute of the [[Council of Italy|Royal Italian Talassografic Committee]] (Council of Italy).

In 1939 Friberti applied for migration into the United States by submitting an application for the Emergency Committee in Aid of Displaced Foreign Scholars.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Rediscovering the Refugee Scholars of the Nazi Era |url=https://www.northeastern.edu/refugeescholars/data |access-date=2023-06-18 |website=Northeastern University}}</ref> Thousands of scholars, including 80 female scientists and mathematicians, applied to this committee during the second World War.<ref name=":2" /> Friberti's application was denied by the committee because it was deemed that she would not have an easy time finding a new job in the United States.<ref name=":1" />

Ultimately, Friberti escaped to Switzerland.<ref>{{Cite web |last=sheldon |first=Natasha |date=6 February 2018 |title=The Scientists History Abandoned: The Cruel Reality of Being a Scholarly Woman or Refugee Fleeing the Holocaust to America |url=https://historycollection.com/scientists-history-abandoned-cruel-reality-scholarly-woman-refugee-fleeing-holocaust-america/ |access-date=2023-06-18 |website=History Collection |language=en-US}}</ref>
